ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the power amplifier shown in the figure, when it is operating normally and the power supply voltage is 12V, what is the voltage at its output midpoint?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a single-supply power amplifier circuit, the upper power rail is labeled +Vcc, and the lower part is grounded; VT1 and VT2 are connected vertically, and the node between the two is located on the left side of the coupling capacitor C. This is the output midpoint, and the right side of the capacitor is connected to the load RL. Then reason: the problem gives the supply voltage Vcc = 12V, and the circuit is working normally. For this kind of single-supply complementary push-pull power amplifier, under normal static bias, the DC voltage at the output midpoint should be Vcc/2, to ensure that the upper and lower swings of the output signal are symmetrical. Therefore the output midpoint voltage = 12V / 2 = 6V.
